newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tap says Harriet field gas goes to Boral.
newsitem.headline: Tap says Harriet field gas goes to Boral.

text.p: Tap Oil NL said on Wednesday the partners in the Harriet gas field offshore Western Australia had finalised an agreement to supply natural gas to Boral Gas (WA) Pty Ltd, a unit of Boral Ltd.
Tap said Boral anticipates using the gas to satisfy its various gas contracts, including supplying gas to the Murrin Murrin nickel project, located near Leonora in Western Australia.

Earlier on Wednesday, the partnership in Murrin Murrin said it had reached a minimum 16-year supply contract with Boral worth A$220 million to supply gas to the project via Goldfields Gas Transmission's Dampier-Kalgoorlie pipeline.
Part of the agreement calls for Boral to build and operate an 80 km gas spur line leading from the pipeline.
The gas is initially to be produced from the developed Harriet field and potentially from the yet-to-be developed Wonmich field, Tap said.
Subject to arrangement being in place for the financing of Murrin Murrin, Tap said gas supplies to Boral will start on April 1, 1998 for a period of 10 years.
Tap holds a 12.2 percent interest in the Harriet Joint Venture through its wholly-owned Tap (Harriet) Pty Ltd.

The other Harriet partners are operator Apache Energy Ltd with 22.5 percent, Mobil Corp 25 percent, Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Corp 19.3 percent, Novus Petroleum Ltd 12.5 percent, Hardy Oil and Gas Plc 8.4 percent and New World Oil Development Pty Ltd with 0.1 percent. Murrin Murrin is 60 percent owned by Anaconda Nickel NL Glencore also holds a 19 percent interest in Anaconda.
The agreement between Boral and the Harriet Joint Venture follows a heads of agreement pact entred into by both parties in March 1997.
